title: Why the Test Pyramid Matters Most

scenes.line1: How should you balance your tests?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why interviewers love asking about the test pyramid? Let’s break down why it’s the single most important idea in software testing.

scenes.label: Unit
scenes.sub: Fast, isolated tests for small pieces of code.
scenes.say: Unit tests are your foundation. They're fast, cheap, and focus on tiny chunks of code in isolation.
Integration tests check how parts work together, but they're slower. End-to-end tests cover user flows, but are slowest and most fragile.
The pyramid means: lots of unit tests, fewer integration, and just a handful of end-to-end tests. This keeps your suite fast and trustworthy.

scenes.question: Should you rely on E2E tests for coverage?
scenes.right: No. E2E tests are flaky and slow. Rely on unit and integration tests for coverage.
scenes.say: Here’s the interview trap: don’t rely on end-to-end tests for coverage. They’re flaky and slow. Unit and integration tests are your real safety net.
